scope: Third-party community posts about LangGraph/LangChain composition failures, excluding the 14 GitHub issues already used in evals/realworld.

sources_attempted.method: Discourse public search.json queries + /raw/<topic_id>/<post> read endpoints; no login
StackExchange API 2.3 search/advanced (tag=langgraph) + questions?filter=withbody; no login

sources_attempted.detail: Hostname resolves to a non-public IP in this environment; no public Reddit result was returned by web_search either. Login/paywall bypass was not attempted.

fetch_policy: Only URLs, metadata and short paraphrased summaries are stored here. Post bodies were read for verification but are not copied into this JSON; no full text lives in raw/community/.
exclusion_policy: Excluded the 14 GitHub issues already used in evals/realworld.
Excluded pure UI/visualization, deployment, pricing, installation and generic how-to posts with no observable failure.
Excluded posts with no discernible graph structure unless they documented a concrete composition symptom (then marked reproducible=partial/no).

candidates.title: InvalidUpdateError: Node __copy__ does not exist - LangGraph State Update Failure
candidates.summary: Calling update_state through the LangGraph API raises InvalidUpdateError: Node __copy__ does not exist; reporter is on LangGraph API 0.4.20 / in-memory runtime 0.12.0. No graph definition was posted.
candidates.notes: Error stack and version info are given, but no graph code; the reply only asks for a minimal repro. Needs a platform/runtime environment, so not fixture-ready yet.

candidates.title: Graph execution goes back to a previous node
candidates.summary: A ReAct-style routing setup unexpectedly re-executes get_product_id and then raises InvalidUpdateError at key 'route': Can receive only one value per step. Only a trace screenshot and the error text were posted.
candidates.notes: Unresolved; the maintainer asked for more code. Likely a routing/loop design issue, but the material cannot confirm it. Useful as a trace-only community report example.

candidates.title: How can parallel nodes send a param value to the same downstream node ? the downstream node needs to adapt the param value based on which parallel upstream node called it
candidates.summary: Two parallel branches call the same downstream save-file helper and need to know which branch they came from. A list reducer merges both branch updates out of order, while removing the reducer raises InvalidUpdateError at key 'last_tool'.
candidates.notes: State snippet included; no accepted answer. Directly exercises parallel-write/reducer reasoning (ACR002-adjacent) plus branch-identity ambiguity; strong fixture candidate.

candidates.title: State is not being copied between sub-graphs
candidates.summary: A subgraph hands off to the next subgraph with Command.PARENT, but updates accumulated earlier in the same stream are missing; only the Command(update=...) payload reaches the parent. The reply says this is expected: state crosses a subgraph boundary only via the returned update.
candidates.notes: Contains State and Command snippets; maintainer-style reply confirms the behavior, so this is a state-design/handoff issue rather than a framework bug. Relevant to Command/Send + subgraph boundary gaps.

candidates.title: Pre-interrupt() code re-runs on resume — anti-pattern, or is there a sanctioned way to detect resume?
candidates.summary: Code before interrupt() runs again on every resume, duplicating log lines and once-per-run verification work. The reply confirms the re-run contract, says there is no public resume-detection flag, and recommends splitting the node or persisting an idempotency marker.
candidates.notes: Documented behavior, not a defect (langgraph 1.1.2, Python 3.12). Valuable boundary case for resume-replay rules: a static rule must not flag intended pre-interrupt code as a bug.

candidates.title: How to modify specific item in a State
candidates.summary: Multiple nodes update different cells of a nested list state in the same step. The OP asks for the canonical pattern, posting parallel node returns and a custom reducer; the reply confirms a reducer is required for parallel updates.
candidates.notes: Code snippet of state + two nodes; no explicit traceback in the OP, so it is mainly a reducer-semantics design question. Has an accepted answer; usable as a reducer fixture seed but failure evidence is indirect.

candidates.title: Restoring to checkpoint doesn't resume from node of checkpoint
candidates.summary: update_state on an older checkpoint_id writes new values, but the new checkpoint inherits next from the thread's latest checkpoint instead of the selected one, so time-travel resume does not continue from the chosen node.
candidates.notes: Concrete API behavior and version context, no code; a reply suggests using a checkpoint object instead of checkpoint_id. Candidate for checkpoint-resume semantics but needs a repro.

candidates.title: Does LangGraph support using HITL within subgraphs?
candidates.summary: interrupt() inside a subgraph invoked from a parent node appears not to pause. The snippet lacks a checkpointer/thread_id, mixes the interrupt payload with the resume value, and misses END edges; the reply lists the required HITL mechanics and notes that function-invoked subgraphs restart on resume.
candidates.notes: Full snippet; the answer identifies several usage errors. Good parallel-interrupt/resume fixture seed if framed as user-graph misuse rather than a framework bug.

candidates.title: Streaming subgraphs results in duplicate messages as subgraph updates parent
candidates.summary: With subgraphs=True streaming, when a subagent completes the router emits its full message list again, so clients see duplicate messages; the OP asks whether filtering is the client's job. No code, but it points at the documented streaming example.
candidates.notes: No code or traceback; behavior may be documented stream semantics. Lower priority; needs reproduction before fixture work.

candidates.title: How to Propagate Parent State to a Compiled Subgraph Triggered via Send API
candidates.summary: Send fan-out to a compiled subgraph does not pass the parent's document_id automatically; adding it to Send args makes parallel siblings write the same parent key and raises INVALID_CONCURRENT_GRAPH_UPDATE. A follow-up post includes graph code and the thread has an accepted answer.
candidates.notes: Code appears in the follow-up post; the answer explains that parent state is not auto-propagated via Send and suggests a reducer, runtime context, or invoke-from-node alternatives. Relevant to declared-keys/state ownership and Send semantics.

candidates.title: LangChain error: Must write to at least one of []
candidates.summary: A node returns a dict keyed 'mesages' (typo for 'messages'); every write is filtered against the declared schema, so the next step raises InvalidUpdateError: Must write to at least one of ['messages'].
candidates.notes: Full code; minimal declared-key mismatch caused by a typo (older langgraph traceback). Low-ambiguity usage fixture, distinct from the first batch's GitHub #2644 class-node/foreign-schema case.

candidates.title: How to implement subgraph memory/persistence in LangGraph when parent and subgraph states diverge?
candidates.summary: When the parent sets a shared field (A=None), the subgraph's checkpointed value is lost; the OP wants subgraphs to keep their own state across parent overrides. The example uses the older Graph API pseudo-code.
candidates.notes: Has an accepted answer; code is pseudo/older API, not directly runnable. Subgraph-isolation/checkpoint question that needs translation to the current StateGraph API before fixture work.

candidates.title: LangGraph KeyError: when embedding a compiled subgraph node in a parent graph workflow
candidates.summary: Registering a compiled subgraph as parent node 'scheduler_assistant' and routing to that node from START raises KeyError: 'scheduler_assistant' inside LangGraph routing. The post includes a minimal structure and the traceback.
candidates.notes: Concrete KeyError plus code fragments; may be a node-name/routing bug on 0.5.x/0.6.7 or graph-construction misuse — unresolved. Good candidate for subgraph-registration diagnostics.

candidates.title: The conditional edge in LangGraph causes the reduce function to be invoked twice
candidates.summary: A looping conditional edge makes an Annotated list reducer append each Fibonacci value twice; the OP expects one reducer call per node update. A full runnable snippet with expected-vs-actual output is included.
candidates.notes: Full code and observed duplicate values; no answer. Root cause unconfirmed (could be conditional-edge write semantics), so verify before labeling it framework vs usage. Directly targets reducer double-application.

candidates.title: The parallel mapReduce task implemented by LangGraph has an incorrect execution order
candidates.summary: With Send fan-out and a deferred node, b2 still waits for the slow sibling c and runs after it, contrary to the OP's expected order. Full async code and timestamped output are included; this looks like superstep-barrier semantics.
candidates.notes: Full code and env (langgraph 0.6.6); no accepted answer. Probably expected scheduling semantics, but a useful reference for the boundary of parallel/execution-order rules.
